##### ---- Carbon-14

```{r carbon_14_kimball_and_christenson}

# First, recreate Kimball and Christenson estimates with new data:

# ============================================================
# Kimball & Christensen (Zion Canyon) carbon-14 age correction
# Two independent methods, computed side by side
# ============================================================
#
# METHOD 1: NETPATH-style mass-balance (mass_balance_correction())
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#   1. Open-system calcite-CO2(g) equilibrium for the "initial"
#      (hypothetical recharge) water at each scenario's assumed
#      soil-zone/atmospheric PCO2 -- confirmed by Kimball &
#      Christensen's methods text: "pure water was equilibrated
#      with varying concentrations of CO2 in equilibrium with
#      calcite... other major ions were not included in the
#      starting water compositions."
#   2. Their published stoichiometric mass-transfer matrix (Table 1:
#      Calcite, Dolomite, Albite, Halite, Gypsum, CO2 vs. Ca, Mg, Na,
#      Cl, S, C) solved via linear algebra (their Equation 1) to get
#      mineral/gas mass-transfer coefficients between the initial
#      and final (sampled) water.
#   3. Isotope mass balance using: mineral pool (calcite + dolomite
#      mass transfer) = 0 pmc, "dead" carbon; modern pool (initial
#      water's own carbon + any additional CO2 gas mass transfer)
#      = 50 pmc, NOT 100 pmc. This 50 pmc value matters and is
#      confirmed directly by their methods text: because the
#      initial water itself forms via CaCO3 + CO2 + H2O -> Ca2+ +
#      2HCO3-, exactly half of ITS OWN carbon is already
#      mineral-derived even before any further flow-path reaction --
#      "the value of And for modern carbon dissolved in ground water
#      with calcite present would be 50 pmc rather than 100 pmc."
#   4. The standard 14C age equation (their Equation 3, 5,730-yr
#      half-life): RT = (5730/ln2) * ln(And/Aobs).
#
#   VALIDATION: checked against the three springs with published
#   results. With pmc_modern = 50, Plateau 1 and Outcrop (both at
#   atmospheric-level PCO2, log = -3.5) now match closely (within
#   ~1-2 pmc of published And_pmc). Plateau 2-4 (elevated soil-zone
#   PCO2) still run higher than published, with the gap widening as
#   PCO2 increases (e.g., Larry's Grotto Plateau 4: 57.3 modeled vs.
#   30.1 published And_pmc). We were not able to fully close this
#   remaining gap -- it may relate to how additional CO2 gas mass
#   transfer along the flow path (beyond the initial recharge
#   equilibration) should be weighted, which we could not verify
#   without the original NETPATH intermediate output. Treat Plateau
#   1/Outcrop results with more confidence than Plateau 2-4.
#   See model_vs_published_comparison.csv for the full comparison.
#
# METHOD 2: Classic Pearson/Ingerson two-endmember (pearson_correction())
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#   A simpler, independent, well-established method that does not
#   require the mass-balance solve at all. It uses the SAMPLE'S OWN
#   measured delta13C directly, positioned between the same two
#   endmembers (mineral delta13C and gas delta13C) used above:
#     q = (delta13C_measured - delta13C_mineral) / (delta13C_gas - delta13C_mineral)
#     And_pmc = q * pmc_modern
#   This does not reproduce the published table either, and is
#   undefined when delta13C_gas == delta13C_mineral (the Outcrop
#   scenario here, where both endmembers are -7 permil) -- a known
#   limitation of the two-endmember approach when the endmembers
#   coincide. It's included as a standard point of comparison, not
#   because it's known to be more correct.
#
# Bottom line: neither method exactly reproduces Kimball &
# Christensen's 1994 published ages. Use both as first-pass
# screening tools on new samples, sanity-checked against geologic
# judgment, not as a validated exact reproduction of the original
# report.
# ============================================================

# ---- 1. Carbonate/calcite equilibrium constants (25 deg C) ----
pK0  <- 1.47   # CO2(g) <-> CO2(aq)
pK1  <- 6.35   # CO2(aq) + H2O <-> H+ + HCO3-
pK2  <- 10.33  # HCO3- <-> H+ + CO3--
pKsp <- 8.48   # calcite: CaCO3(s) <-> Ca2+ + CO3--

K0  <- 10^-pK0
K1  <- 10^-pK1
K2  <- 10^-pK2
Ksp <- 10^-pKsp

HALF_LIFE <- 5730  # 14C half-life, years (Kimball & Christensen Eq. 3)

# ---- 2. "Initial" (pre-reaction, hypothetical recharge) water ----
# Open-system calcite dissolution: water equilibrated with soil/atm
# CO2 at a given log10(PCO2), then dissolves calcite to saturation.
# Charge balance simplifies (dilute, near-neutral pH) to 2[Ca] = [HCO3-],
# giving the classic cube-root PCO2 dependence for [HCO3-].
initial_water <- function(logPCO2) {
  pco2  <- 10^logPCO2
  co2aq <- K0 * pco2
  hco3  <- (2 * Ksp * K1 * co2aq / K2)^(1/3)
  ca    <- hco3 / 2
  dic   <- hco3 + co2aq
  list(Ca_mM = ca * 1000, C_mM = dic * 1000)  # mol/L -> mmol/L
}

# ---- 3. Stoichiometric matrix (Kimball & Christensen Table 1) ----
stoich <- matrix(
  c(1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0,    # Calcium
    0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0,    # Magnesium
    0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0,    # Sodium
    0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0,    # Chloride
    0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0,    # Sulfur
    1, 2, 0, 0, 0, 1),   # Carbon
  nrow = 6, byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(
    c("Ca", "Mg", "Na", "Cl", "S", "C"),
    c("Calcite", "Dolomite", "Albite", "Halite", "Gypsum", "CO2")
  )
)

solve_mass_transfer <- function(delta_m) {
  delta_m <- delta_m[c("Ca", "Mg", "Na", "Cl", "S", "C")]
  a <- solve(stoich, delta_m)
  names(a) <- colnames(stoich)
  a
}

# ============================================================
# METHOD 1: mass-balance correction
# ============================================================
# final_chem: named numeric vector c(Ca_mM=, Mg_mM=, Na_mM=, Cl_mM=,
#             SO4_mM=, C_mM=) for the sampled spring water
# pmc_modern: 14C activity assumed for the "modern" carbon pool.
#             Default 50 (not 100) -- see notes above; the initial
#             water is itself already a 50/50 mix of gas- and
#             mineral-derived carbon by the calcite-CO2 reaction
#             stoichiometry, so the whole "modern" pool (initial
#             water carbon + any additional CO2 gas mass transfer)
#             is best represented at 50 pmc, not 100 pmc.
mass_balance_correction <- function(final_chem, logPCO2, c13_min, c13_gas,
                                     c14_pmc_measured, pmc_modern = 50) {
  iw <- initial_water(logPCO2)
  delta_m <- c(
    Ca = final_chem["Ca_mM"] - iw$Ca_mM,
    Mg = final_chem["Mg_mM"],
    Na = final_chem["Na_mM"],
    Cl = final_chem["Cl_mM"],
    S  = final_chem["SO4_mM"],
    C  = final_chem["C_mM"] - iw$C_mM
  )
  names(delta_m) <- c("Ca", "Mg", "Na", "Cl", "S", "C")
  a_p <- solve_mass_transfer(delta_m)

  mineral_C <- unname(a_p["Calcite"] + 2 * a_p["Dolomite"])
  modern_C  <- unname(iw$C_mM + a_p["CO2"])
  total_C   <- mineral_C + modern_C

  c13_calculated <- (modern_C * c13_gas + mineral_C * c13_min) / total_C
  and_pmc        <- (modern_C * pmc_modern) / total_C

  age <- if (!is.na(and_pmc) && and_pmc > 0) {
    (HALF_LIFE / log(2)) * log(and_pmc / c14_pmc_measured)
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }

  list(
    Ca_initial_mM = iw$Ca_mM, C_initial_mM = iw$C_mM,
    a_calcite = unname(a_p["Calcite"]), a_dolomite = unname(a_p["Dolomite"]),
    a_CO2 = unname(a_p["CO2"]), mineral_C = mineral_C, modern_C = modern_C,
    C13_calculated = unname(c13_calculated), And_pmc = unname(and_pmc),
    C14_age_corrected = age
  )
}

# ============================================================
# METHOD 2: classic Pearson/Ingerson two-endmember correction
# ============================================================
# c13_measured: the SAMPLE'S OWN measured delta13C (permil)
# c13_min, c13_gas: assumed delta13C endmembers for this scenario
# pmc_modern: 14C activity assumed for the fully "modern" endmember.
#             Default 50 for consistency with Method 1's finding
#             above; the classic literature default is 100 -- try
#             both and compare.
pearson_correction <- function(c13_measured, c13_min, c13_gas,
                                c14_pmc_measured, pmc_modern = 50) {
  if (c13_gas == c13_min) {
    return(list(q = NA_real_, And_pmc = NA_real_, C14_age_corrected = NA_real_))
  }
  q <- (c13_measured - c13_min) / (c13_gas - c13_min)
  and_pmc <- q * pmc_modern
  age <- if (!is.na(and_pmc) && and_pmc > 0) {
    (HALF_LIFE / log(2)) * log(and_pmc / c14_pmc_measured)
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
  list(q = q, And_pmc = and_pmc, C14_age_corrected = age)
}

# ============================================================
# 4. Apply both methods to Zion Canyon spring data, compare to published
# ============================================================
final_chem <- read.csv("data/park/ZION/Carbon_14/final_water_chemistry_mmolL.csv",
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
scenarios  <- read.csv("data/park/ZION/Carbon_14/scenario_definitions.csv",
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
published  <- read.csv("data/park/ZION/Carbon_14/kimball_christensen_published_table.csv",
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

results <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(final_chem))) {
  site <- final_chem$site[i]
  fc <- as.numeric(final_chem[i, c("Ca_mM", "Mg_mM", "Na_mM", "Cl_mM", "SO4_mM", "C_mM")])
  names(fc) <- c("Ca_mM", "Mg_mM", "Na_mM", "Cl_mM", "SO4_mM", "C_mM")

  for (j in seq_len(nrow(scenarios))) {
    scen <- scenarios[j, ]
    pub_row <- published[published$Site == site & published$Scenario == scen$scenario, ]
    if (nrow(pub_row) == 0) next
    c14m <- pub_row$C14_pmc[1]
    c13m <- pub_row$C13_permil[1]

    mb <- mass_balance_correction(fc, scen$logPCO2atm, scen$c13_dissolving_minerals,
                                   scen$c13_gas, c14m)
    pe <- pearson_correction(c13m, scen$c13_dissolving_minerals, scen$c13_gas, c14m)

    results[[length(results) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      site = site, scenario = scen$scenario, logPCO2atm = scen$logPCO2atm,
      proxy_chem_group = NA_character_,
      And_pmc_massbalance = round(mb$And_pmc, 1),
      C14_age_massbalance = round(mb$C14_age_corrected, 0),
      And_pmc_pearson = round(pe$And_pmc, 1),
      C14_age_pearson = round(pe$C14_age_corrected, 0),
      And_pmc_published = pub_row$And_pmc[1],
      C14_age_published = pub_row$C14_age_corrected[1],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }
}

# ============================================================
# 5. Extend to newly collected field samples (Lower Grotto, East Entrance
#    Well) -- 14C/13C only, no site-specific major-ion chemistry available
#    yet. The mass-balance method needs a "final_chem" input, so bracket the
#    missing chemistry with two proxy groups drawn from the original four
#    springs' own chemistry, which separate cleanly into a high-TDS
#    ("saline") pair and a low-TDS ("dilute") pair:
#
#    CAVEAT (added after re-reading Kimball & Christensen 1996 directly):
#    the saline/dilute split here is not just a chemistry-availability
#    workaround, it maps onto two hydrologically distinct flow paths in the
#    paper -- plateau recharge through the Carmel Formation (their Path A,
#    conductivity >1,000 uS/cm: Larry's Grotto, Weeping Rock) versus local
#    recharge straight into the Navajo Sandstone (their Path B, <300-400
#    uS/cm: The Grotto, Refrigerator Spring). The paper states plainly that
#    the NETPATH mass-balance framework did NOT produce a plausible model
#    for either Path B site ("none of the models... matched the observed
#    d13C value"; "there were no plausible models"). Both new 2025 samples
#    (East Entrance Well: 394 uS/cm; Lower Grotto: 322 uS/cm) are, by their
#    own measured conductivity, Path B water -- so bracketing them against
#    the Path A ("saline") chemistry below is very likely applying a model
#    to water it was never meant to describe, which is a plausible
#    explanation for why most of these scenario/proxy combinations return
#    non-physical negative ages further down. The loop below is kept as a
#    sensitivity/diagnostic run (useful for seeing HOW badly a Path A model
#    fits Path B water), but `c14_age_summary` in the error-bars chunk no
#    longer uses these results for its central estimate -- see that chunk
#    for the Path A/B-aware replacement.
# ============================================================
proxy_chem_groups <- list(
  saline = c("Larry's Grotto", "Weeping Rock"),
  dilute = c("Refrigerator Spring", "The Grotto")
)

proxy_chem <- purrr::imap_dfr(proxy_chem_groups, function(sites, grp) {
  final_chem %>%
    dplyr::filter(site %in% sites) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(c(Ca_mM, Mg_mM, Na_mM, Cl_mM, SO4_mM, C_mM), mean)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(proxy_group = grp, .before = 1)
})

new_field_samples <- c("Lower Grotto", "East Entrance Well")

for (site in new_field_samples) {
  pub_rows <- published[published$Site == site, ]
  if (nrow(pub_rows) == 0) next
  c14m <- pub_rows$C14_pmc[1]
  c13m <- pub_rows$C13_permil[1]

  for (j in seq_len(nrow(scenarios))) {
    scen <- scenarios[j, ]
    pe <- pearson_correction(c13m, scen$c13_dissolving_minerals, scen$c13_gas, c14m)

    for (grp in names(proxy_chem_groups)) {
      fc_row <- proxy_chem[proxy_chem$proxy_group == grp, ]
      fc <- as.numeric(fc_row[, c("Ca_mM", "Mg_mM", "Na_mM", "Cl_mM", "SO4_mM", "C_mM")])
      names(fc) <- c("Ca_mM", "Mg_mM", "Na_mM", "Cl_mM", "SO4_mM", "C_mM")

      mb <- mass_balance_correction(fc, scen$logPCO2atm, scen$c13_dissolving_minerals,
                                     scen$c13_gas, c14m)

      results[[length(results) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        site = site, scenario = scen$scenario, logPCO2atm = scen$logPCO2atm,
        proxy_chem_group = grp,
        And_pmc_massbalance = round(mb$And_pmc, 1),
        C14_age_massbalance = round(mb$C14_age_corrected, 0),
        And_pmc_pearson = round(pe$And_pmc, 1),
        C14_age_pearson = round(pe$C14_age_corrected, 0),
        And_pmc_published = NA_real_,
        C14_age_published = NA_real_,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  }
}

comparison <- do.call(rbind, results)
print(comparison)

kable(comparison) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center"
  ) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, background = "#f2f2f2") # Highlight header row

write.csv(comparison, "data/park/ZION/Carbon_14/method_comparison_both_R.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```

##### ---- Carbon-14 Error Bars

```{r carbon_14_error_bars}
# ============================================================
# Error bars on corrected carbon-14 ages
# ============================================================
# REVISED after re-reading Kimball & Christensen (1996) directly: ages are
# now only computed for the two sites the paper's own NETPATH framework
# actually applies to (Path A -- Larry's Grotto, Weeping Rock). See "Site
# classification" below for why, and the previous version of this chunk
# (git history) for the earlier median-of-valid-mass-balance-scenarios
# approach this replaces.
#
# Two uncertainty tiers, kept visually distinct rather than combined into
# one number, since they represent different things:
#
#   INNER (bold, black) bar: analytical/lab counting uncertainty on the
#   measured pMC itself, propagated through the age equation
#   RT = (T/ln2)*ln(And/Aobs). Because d(age)/d(Aobs) = -(T/ln2)/Aobs does
#   not depend on And, this works out to a fixed +/- age width per site.
#   Only available where a lab-reported pMC counting error exists; the two
#   Path A sites (1988-89 samples) have no stated analytical uncertainty in
#   the source data, so they get no inner bar. (delta13C analytical
#   uncertainty was considered and intentionally left out, both because
#   it isn't available for the new samples and for consistency with the
#   original four springs, which also lack it.)
#
#   OUTER (light gray) whisker: the full published min-to-max spread across
#   Plateau 1-4/Outcrop for the two Path A sites. This is a modeling/
#   assumption uncertainty, not a statistical one -- shown as the literal
#   range, not a symmetric error bar. Path B sites have no whisker at all:
#   per K&C 1996 no scenario in this framework is a plausible model for
#   them (see below), so there's no range to show.

HALF_LIFE_YR <- 5730

# Lab-reported +/- pMC counting uncertainty. This data collection only --
# not available for the original four springs.
pmc_lab_error <- tibble::tibble(
  site = c("Lower Grotto", "East Entrance Well"),
  pmc_error = c(0.21, 0.30)
)

# One measured pMC per site (constant across that site's 5 scenario rows
# in `published`).
measured_pmc <- published %>%
  dplyr::distinct(site = Site, pmc_measured = C14_pmc)

analytical_age_error <- pmc_lab_error %>%
  dplyr::left_join(measured_pmc, by = "site") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_error_analytical = (HALF_LIFE_YR / log(2)) * (pmc_error / pmc_measured)
  )

# ---- Site classification: Path A (plateau) vs Path B (local) -------------
# Kimball & Christensen (1996) split sites into two hydrologically distinct
# groups by conductivity, not by which geochemical scenario fits best: a
# high-conductivity (>1,000 uS/cm) group recharged on the plateau tops and
# routed through the marine Carmel Formation (their Path A -- Larry's
# Grotto, Weeping Rock), where the NETPATH mass-balance framework applies;
# and a low-conductivity group recharged locally, straight into the Navajo
# Sandstone (their Path B -- The Grotto, Refrigerator Spring), for which
# they state plainly that no plausible mass-balance model exists at all.
# Classifying by each site's own measured conductivity -- rather than by
# which two "template" sites' chemistry a new sample gets bracketed
# against -- is what puts East Entrance Well (394 uS/cm) and Lower Grotto
# (322 uS/cm) in Path B alongside The Grotto/Refrigerator Spring instead of
# treating them as ambiguous between the two groups.
site_conductivity <- zion_samples %>%
  group_by(location) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(cond_mean = mean(cond, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(site = dplyr::if_else(location == "Lower Grotto Sandtrap", "Lower Grotto", location))

site_path <- site_conductivity %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    flow_path = dplyr::if_else(cond_mean >= 1000,
                                "Path A (plateau/saline)",
                                "Path B (local/dilute)")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(site, cond_mean, flow_path)

site_path

# ---- Path A: central estimate from the paper's own preferred scenario ----
# K&C state directly: "Both models suggest soil-zone CO2 near 10^-2.25 atm,
# which is a reasonable value between scenarios 3 and 4" -- i.e. their
# actual preferred answer sits BETWEEN Plateau 3 (log PCO2 = -2.5) and
# Plateau 4 (-2.0), not at any one of the five tabulated scenarios. Their
# stated "likely residence times" (Larry's Grotto ~4,100 yr, Weeping Rock
# ~1,200 yr) match the average of the two PUBLISHED Plateau 3/4 ages almost
# exactly (4,200 and 1,280) -- used here as age_central. Deliberately using
# the PUBLISHED ages rather than our own mass-balance reconstruction for
# this central estimate: the reconstruction is already flagged above as
# running systematically higher than published for Plateau 2-4, an
# unresolved gap, which would bias the "most likely" estimate in exactly
# the scenario range we trust it least. Plateau 1, Plateau 2, and Outcrop
# are the less-likely bookends -- their published ages set the outer
# uncertainty range, not the center.
path_a_ages <- published %>%
  dplyr::filter(Site %in% c("Larry's Grotto", "Weeping Rock")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(site = Site) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(site) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    age_central       = mean(C14_age_corrected[Scenario %in% c("Plateau 3", "Plateau 4")]),
    age_scenario_min  = min(C14_age_corrected),
    age_scenario_max  = max(C14_age_corrected),
    n_scenarios_total = dplyr::n(),
    n_scenarios_valid = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(valid_label = paste0(n_scenarios_valid, "/", n_scenarios_total))

# ---- Path B: no plausible NETPATH model (K&C 1996) ------------------------
# The Grotto's row in kimball_christensen_published_table.csv has
# C14_age_corrected hardcoded to 0 for all five scenarios -- checked against
# the paper text, this is a data-entry placeholder for "not calculated," not
# a real corrected age of zero (the paper: "None of the models for water
# from The Grotto matched the observed d13C value; thus, age corrections
# could not be calculated"). Treated as NA here, same as Refrigerator
# Spring (already blank in the source table) and the two new Path B
# samples, so all four get identical, honest "no age" treatment rather than
# The Grotto silently looking like a resolved "modern" (age = 0) result.
path_b_sites <- c("The Grotto", "Refrigerator Spring", "East Entrance Well", "Lower Grotto")
path_b_ages <- tibble::tibble(
  site               = path_b_sites,
  age_central        = NA_real_,
  age_scenario_min   = NA_real_,
  age_scenario_max   = NA_real_,
  n_scenarios_total  = 5L,
  n_scenarios_valid  = 0L,
  valid_label        = "Path B — no plausible NETPATH model (K&C 1996)"
)

c14_age_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(path_a_ages, path_b_ages) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(site_path, by = "site") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(analytical_age_error, site, age_error_analytical), by = "site") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_analytical_min = pmax(age_central - age_error_analytical, 0),
    age_analytical_max = age_central + age_error_analytical
  )

c14_age_summary

# ---- Tritium-constrained mixing check (sensitivity analysis) --------------
# The age equation above assumes the whole sampled parcel is "old" water
# that lost contact with the atmosphere at one point in time (Aobs =
# And*exp(-lambda*t)). K&C's own tritium discussion raises a different
# possibility for these same two springs: "Weeping Rock has higher 3H
# values than the Grotto or Refrigerator Spring. This likely reflects some
# mixing of modern and older waters... some of the waters may represent a
# mixture of modern and old waters." We already have an independent
# estimate of that modern fraction from the tritium mixing model
# (`young_frac_mean`) -- this uses it to test the single-age assumption
# instead of just asserting it.
#
# Binary mixing: Aobs = f*A_modern + (1-f)*And*exp(-lambda*t_old), solved
# for the "old" component's age:
#   t_old = (T_half/ln2) * ln( And*(1-f) / (Aobs - f*A_modern) )
# f = 0 recovers the standard (no-mixing) equation exactly. Undefined (NA)
# whenever the modern contribution implied by f alone would already exceed
# the total observed activity (Aobs - f*A_modern <= 0) -- that outcome is
# itself informative, not just a computational edge case (see note below).
A_MODERN_PMC <- 100  # fully modern/atmospheric 14C activity, pmc

mixing_corrected_age <- function(and_pmc, aobs_pmc, f_young, a_modern = A_MODERN_PMC) {
  if (any(is.na(c(and_pmc, aobs_pmc, f_young)))) return(NA_real_)
  denominator <- aobs_pmc - f_young * a_modern
  if (denominator <= 0) return(NA_real_)
  (HALF_LIFE_YR / log(2)) * log(and_pmc * (1 - f_young) / denominator)
}

mixing_check <- published %>%
  dplyr::filter(Site %in% c("Larry's Grotto", "Weeping Rock"),
                Scenario %in% c("Plateau 3", "Plateau 4")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(site = Site) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(site) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    and_pmc_used = mean(And_pmc),
    aobs_pmc     = dplyr::first(C14_pmc),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    tritium_young_frac_by_location %>%
      dplyr::rename(site = location) %>%
      dplyr::select(site, young_frac_mean),
    by = "site"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_no_mixing   = (HALF_LIFE_YR / log(2)) * log(and_pmc_used / aobs_pmc),
    age_with_mixing = purrr::pmap_dbl(
      list(and_pmc_used, aobs_pmc, young_frac_mean),
      mixing_corrected_age
    ),
    age_shift = age_with_mixing - age_no_mixing
  )

mixing_check

# NOTE on reading mixing_check once rendered: for Weeping Rock, young_frac_mean
# (~0.73 from the tritium mixing model) is large enough that f*A_MODERN_PMC
# alone likely exceeds the site's observed pMC (~28.7) -- i.e. the tritium
# model's own modern-fraction estimate is not quantitatively reconcilable
# with the measured carbon-14 activity under this simple two-component
# model, and age_with_mixing will come back NA rather than a number. That is
# not a bug: the tritium young-fraction estimate is already documented
# above (tritium_mixing_model chunk) as a conservative UPPER bound (it uses
# the minimum post-peak modern threshold), so this is a real tension between
# the two tracers worth flagging rather than silently resolving one way.
# For Larry's Grotto, where young_frac_mean is much smaller (~0.10), expect
# age_with_mixing to come back well ABOVE age_no_mixing: even a small modern
# admixture means the "old" component underneath it must be older than the
# no-mixing calculation assumed, since some of the observed activity is
# being (correctly) attributed to recent recharge instead of decay.

# Sites with a resolvable (>=1 valid scenario) age get the normal
# point + two-tier bars; zero-valid sites are labeled separately below.
c14_age_plottable <- c14_age_summary %>% dplyr::filter(n_scenarios_valid > 0)
c14_age_unresolved <- c14_age_summary %>% dplyr::filter(n_scenarios_valid == 0)

carbon14_error_plot <- ggplot(c14_age_summary, aes(x = reorder(site, dplyr::coalesce(age_central, 0)), y = age_central)) +
  # Outer tier: full published scenario range (Path A sites only)
  geom_errorbar(data = c14_age_plottable,
                aes(ymin = age_scenario_min, ymax = age_scenario_max),
                width = 0.15, color = "gray60", linewidth = 0.7) +
  # Inner tier: analytical/lab pMC uncertainty -- NA for both Path A sites
  # (no lab-reported error for the 1988-89 samples), so geom_errorbar
  # silently skips these rows; kept here in case a future Path A sample
  # does have one.
  geom_errorbar(data = c14_age_plottable,
                aes(ymin = age_analytical_min, ymax = age_analytical_max),
                width = 0.25, color = "black", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = c14_age_plottable, size = 3) +
  # Retained-scenario fraction (5/5 for both Path A sites) next to each point
  geom_text(data = c14_age_plottable, aes(label = valid_label, y = age_scenario_max),
            hjust = -0.3, size = 3.2, color = "gray30") +
  # Path B sites: no plausible NETPATH model, labeled explicitly at x = 0
  # instead of silently vanishing from the plot.
  geom_text(data = c14_age_unresolved, aes(y = 0, label = valid_label),
            hjust = 0, size = 3.2, color = "tomato", fontface = "italic") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Carbon-14 corrected age (years)",
       title = "Carbon-14 corrected age by site, mass-balance method",
       subtitle = "Point: average of published Plateau 3/4 ages (K&C's stated preferred CO2 range). Gray: full published scenario range (Plateau 1-4, Outcrop). Path B (local/dilute) sites have no plausible NETPATH model per K&C 1996.") +
  theme_bw()

carbon14_error_plot

ggsave(plot = carbon14_error_plot,
       filename = "data/park/ZION/Carbon_14/c14_age_error_bars.png", dpi = 300, width = 9, height = 5)
```


```{r carbon_14}

# Carbon-14-corrected ages for the same field samples, derived from the
# `zion_samples` master table read once in the tritium chunk above (not
# re-read from disk here).
c14_nps <-
  zion_samples %>%
  drop_na(c14_corr_age) %>%
  select(location, date, c14_corr_age, cond, latitude, longitude) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

# `tritium_young_frac_by_location` (one row per location, computed in the
# tritium_mixing_model chunk above) joins cleanly onto this multi-row
# carbon-14 table -- a one-to-many join. Joining the two RAW, multi-row
# tables on `location` alone would instead cross every tritium row against
# every carbon-14 row for that location (a many-to-many/cartesian join),
# silently inflating the row count -- hence summarizing tritium first.
c14_nps <- c14_nps %>%
  left_join(tritium_young_frac_by_location, by = "location")

mapview(park_boundary, alpha.regions = 0, color = "black", lwd = 3) +
  mapview(nps_joints, color = "gray30") +
  mapview(nps_faults, color = "black") +
mapview(c14_nps,
        zcol = "c14_corr_age")

# ---- C14 age (with error bars) vs tritium young fraction ------------------
# Uses `c14_age_summary` (built in the carbon_14_error_bars chunk above),
# now Path A/B-aware: only Larry's Grotto and Weeping Rock carry a
# published, geologically-defensible age (n_scenarios_valid = 5/5 for
# both). The other four sites (Path B: The Grotto, Refrigerator Spring,
# East Entrance Well, Lower Grotto) have no plausible NETPATH model at all
# per K&C 1996, so they get no real x-position -- but rather than dropping
# them from the plot entirely, they're placed at a fixed flagged position
# to the left of a dashed "0 years" reference line, with an open/cross
# point shape (vs. Path A's filled circles) so they read as "no age, shown
# for reference" rather than as comparable data points on the same age
# scale.
c14_vs_young_frac <- c14_age_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_scenarios_valid > 0) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    tritium_young_frac_by_location %>%
      dplyr::select(location, young_frac_mean, young_frac_min, young_frac_max) %>%
      dplyr::rename(site = location),
    by = "site"
  ) %>%
  drop_na(young_frac_mean)

# Flagged position for Path B sites: a fixed offset to the left of 0,
# scaled off the Path A age range so it stays clearly separated from the
# real error bars regardless of what those ages happen to be.
flag_x <- -0.15 * max(c14_vs_young_frac$age_scenario_max, na.rm = TRUE)

c14_vs_young_frac_pathB <- c14_age_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_scenarios_valid == 0) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    tritium_young_frac_by_location %>%
      dplyr::mutate(site = dplyr::if_else(location == "Lower Grotto Sandtrap", "Lower Grotto", location)) %>%
      dplyr::select(site, young_frac_mean, young_frac_min, young_frac_max),
    by = "site"
  ) %>%
  drop_na(young_frac_mean) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(age_flag_x = flag_x)

c14_vs_young_frac_plot <- ggplot(c14_vs_young_frac, aes(x = age_central, y = young_frac_mean, color = site)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "gray70") +
  # Path B: flagged markers, no real x-position -- drawn first so Path A's
  # real points/bars sit on top.
  geom_errorbar(data = c14_vs_young_frac_pathB, inherit.aes = FALSE,
                aes(x = age_flag_x, ymin = young_frac_min, ymax = young_frac_max, color = site),
                width = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = c14_vs_young_frac_pathB, inherit.aes = FALSE,
             aes(x = age_flag_x, y = young_frac_mean, color = site),
             shape = 4, size = 3, stroke = 1.3) +
  # Path A: real ages, filled circles
  # Tritium young-fraction range (unchanged from before)
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = young_frac_min, ymax = young_frac_max), width = 0.2) +
  # Outer tier: full published Plateau 1-4/Outcrop scenario range
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = age_scenario_min, xmax = age_scenario_max), height = 0.02, color = "gray50") +
  # Inner tier: analytical pMC uncertainty -- NA for both Path A sites (see
  # error-bar chunk), kept for consistency with the other two plots.
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = age_analytical_min, xmax = age_analytical_max), height = 0.03, linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = flag_x, y = 1.06, label = "No C14 age\n(no plausible model)",
            size = 3, color = "gray40", hjust = 0.5, fontface = "italic") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.12), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0))) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c(
    "Larry's Grotto"       = "dodgerblue",
    "Weeping Rock"         = "seagreen",
    "The Grotto"           = "tomato",
    "Refrigerator Spring"  = "goldenrod",
    "East Entrance Well"   = "orchid",
    "Lower Grotto"         = "gray40"
  )) +
  labs(x = "Carbon-14 corrected age (years)",
       y = "Fraction Young Water (Tritium)",
       title = "Carbon-14 age vs. tritium young fraction, all sites",
       subtitle = stringr::str_wrap(
         "Filled circles (right of dashed line): Path A sites with a published, geologically-defensible age. X markers (left of dashed line): Path B sites -- no plausible NETPATH model per Kimball & Christensen (1996), plotted at a flagged position rather than a real age.",
         width = 100
       ))

c14_vs_young_frac_plot

```



```{r conductivity}


# Plot cond against tritium young frac. Conductivity error bars are the
# min-max range of repeat conductivity measurements at each location (same
# logic as the tritium young-fraction range) -- this reflects real
# site-to-site sampling variability, not sensor/lab analytical uncertainty,
# which we don't have a stated value for. Locations with only one sampled
# date will have a zero-width conductivity bar, same as already happens for
# the young-fraction range in that case.
tritium_nps %>%
  group_by(location) %>%
  drop_na(young_fraction_capped) %>%
  summarize(
    cond = mean(cond, na.rm = TRUE),
    cond_min = min(cond, na.rm = TRUE),
    cond_max = max(cond, na.rm = TRUE),
    young_frac_mean = mean(young_fraction_capped, na.rm = TRUE),
    young_frac_max = max(young_fraction_capped, na.rm = TRUE),
    young_fraction_min = min(young_fraction_capped, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = cond, y = young_frac_mean, color = location)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = young_fraction_min, ymax = young_frac_max),
    width = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(xmin = cond_min, xmax = cond_max),
    height = 0.02
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("lightpink",
                                    "tomato",
                                    "dodgerblue",
                                    "yellow4",
                                    "seagreen",
                                    "navy",
                                    "hotpink",
                                    "gray",
                                    "black"
                                    )) +
  labs(x = "Conductivity",
       y = "Fraction Young Water (Tritium)")

```

##### ---- Multi-Line-of-Evidence Summary

```{r c14_evidence_table}
# ============================================================
# Multi-line-of-evidence summary table
# ============================================================
# One row per site with data across all three lines of evidence used above
# (carbon-14 age or Path B "no model" status, tritium classification/young
# fraction, conductivity) -- lets the Path A/Path B grouping implied by
# conductivity be sanity-checked visually against the two independent
# tracers before relating any of this to mapped geology (faults, formation
# contacts, flow paths) in the next section. Cell shading uses an
# independent color scale PER COLUMN (viridis-based, via
# kableExtra::spec_color) -- colors are only meaningful for comparing
# within a column, not across columns.

evidence_sites <- c("Larry's Grotto", "Weeping Rock", "The Grotto",
                     "Refrigerator Spring", "East Entrance Well", "Lower Grotto")

evidence_table <- c14_age_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(site, flow_path, age_central, valid_label) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    tritium_young_frac_by_location %>%
      dplyr::mutate(site = dplyr::if_else(location == "Lower Grotto Sandtrap", "Lower Grotto", location)) %>%
      dplyr::select(site, tritium_category, young_frac_mean),
    by = "site"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(site_conductivity, site, cond_mean), by = "site") %>%
  dplyr::filter(site %in% evidence_sites) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    c14_age_display = dplyr::if_else(is.na(age_central), valid_label, as.character(round(age_central))),
    pct_modern_display = scales::percent(young_frac_mean, accuracy = 1)
  )

# Independent viridis palettes per numeric column; Path B's NA ages shaded
# flat gray rather than colored (there's no value to encode).
#
# format = "html" is set explicitly below (both cell_spec() and kable())
# rather than left to auto-detect. cell_spec()/kable() normally infer the
# output format from knitr::opts_current$get("format"), which only resolves
# during an actual Knit -- running this chunk interactively (rather than
# knitting the .Rmd) returns nothing, so cell_spec() silently falls back to
# plain text and the HTML/style markup prints literally instead of
# rendering as colored cells. Since this doc's YAML is output: html_document,
# hardcoding "html" here makes the color rendering work identically whether
# you knit or just run the chunk inline in RStudio.
age_pal  <- function(x) kableExtra::spec_color(x, na_color = "grey85", option = "C", direction = -1)
mix_pal  <- function(x) kableExtra::spec_color(x, na_color = "grey85", option = "D")
cond_pal <- function(x) kableExtra::spec_color(x, na_color = "grey85", option = "B")

evidence_table_display <- evidence_table %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Site = site,
    `Flow Path (K&C 1996)` = flow_path,
    `C14 Age (yr)` = kableExtra::cell_spec(
      c14_age_display, format = "html",
      background = age_pal(age_central), color = "black"
    ),
    `Tritium Category` = tritium_category,
    `% Modern Mixing (Tritium)` = kableExtra::cell_spec(
      pct_modern_display, format = "html",
      background = mix_pal(young_frac_mean), color = "black"
    ),
    `Conductivity (µS/cm)` = kableExtra::cell_spec(
      round(cond_mean), format = "html",
      background = cond_pal(cond_mean), color = "black"
    )
  )

kable(evidence_table_display, format = "html", escape = FALSE,
      caption = "Multi-line-of-evidence summary: carbon-14, tritium, and conductivity by site") %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center"
  ) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, background = "#f2f2f2")

```

##### ---- Spatial Distribution vs. Geology

```{r c14_tritium_cond_geology_maps}
# ============================================================
# Spatial distribution of carbon-14 age, tritium mixing, and specific
# conductivity against Navajo Sandstone extent, joints, and faults
# ============================================================
# Point layer built directly from `zion_samples`'s own latitude/longitude
# (crs 4326, one row per sample/date) rather than reusing `c14_nps` or
# `tritium_nps`, since neither carries all three variables in one place:
# `tritium_nps` has no coordinates at all, and `c14_nps` only has
# c14_corr_age. The tritium mixing-model result (young_fraction_capped) is
# joined in from `tritium_nps` (computed in the tritium_mixing_model chunk)
# by location+date, since `zion_samples` itself only carries raw tritium,
# not the mixing-model output.
#
# Navajo Sandstone footprint reuses the same GLG_SYM codes (`navajo`) and
# `nps_geo`/`nps_faults`/`nps_joints` layers imported in Section 4 -- not
# re-read from disk here.
#
# tmap v4 syntax (per the pattern used elsewhere in this repo, e.g.
# site_fig): fill color for polygons/points is now a distinct `fill`
# aesthetic (not `col`, which is now border/outline color for
# polygons/points, and remains line color for tm_lines); continuous
# aesthetics use `fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(...)` /
# `col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(...)` instead of v3's
# `palette=`/`style = "cont"`, with the legend title moved into
# `fill.legend = tm_legend(title = ...)`. The basemap comes from
# `tm_basemap()` (built into tmap v4, works in "plot" mode) rather than
# manually fetching tiles via {maptiles}. All layers are explicitly
# transformed to 3857 (Web Mercator) to match the basemap tiles, and every
# tm_shape() is pinned to the same `geology_aoi` bbox so the three maps'
# extents line up regardless of each layer's own native extent.

zion_samples_sf <- zion_samples %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    tritium_nps %>% 
      dplyr::select(location, date, young_fraction_capped),
    by = c("location", "date")
  ) %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) %>%
  sf::st_transform(3857)

navajo_geo <- nps_geo %>%
  dplyr::filter(GLG_SYM %in% navajo) %>%
  sf::st_transform(3857)

temple_cap_geo <- nps_geo %>%
  dplyr::filter(GLG_SYM %in% temple_cap) %>%
  sf::st_transform(3857)

carmel_geo <- nps_geo %>%
  dplyr::filter(GLG_SYM %in% carmel) %>%
  sf::st_transform(3857)

nps_joints_3857 <- nps_joints %>% sf::st_transform(3857)
nps_faults_3857 <- nps_faults %>% sf::st_transform(3857)
park_boundary_3857 <- park_boundary %>% sf::st_transform(3857)

geology_aoi <- zion_samples_sf %>% 
  sf::st_buffer(7000) %>% 
  sf::st_bbox()
sample_aoi <- st_bbox(zion_samples_sf %>% 
                        dplyr::filter(!is.na(c14_corr_age)) %>%
                        st_buffer(3000)) 


tmap::tmap_mode("plot")

# 1. Combine formation shapes into a single sf object
formations_sf <- rbind(
  navajo_geo %>% mutate(formation = "Navajo"),
  temple_cap_geo %>% mutate(formation = "Temple Cap"),
  carmel_geo %>% mutate(formation = "Carmel")
)

# 2. Combine line features into a single sf object
structures_sf <- rbind(
  nps_joints_3857 %>% mutate(structure = "Joints"),
  nps_faults_3857 %>% mutate(structure = "Faults")
)

# Shared base layers
geology_base <-
  # Basemap
  tm_basemap("Esri.WorldTopoMap") +
  
  # Geologic Formations
  tm_shape(formations_sf, bbox = sample_aoi) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "formation",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(
      values = formation_colors
#        c(
#        "Navajo Sandstone" = "pink4", 
#        "Temple Cap" = "dodgerblue", 
#        "Carmel" = "darkblue"
 #     )
    ),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Formation"),
    fill_alpha = 0.4,
    col = NA,
    lwd = 0
  ) +
  
  # Structural Features (Joints & Faults)
  tm_shape(structures_sf, bbox = geology_aoi) +
  tm_lines(
    col = "structure",
    col.scale = tm_scale_categorical(
      values = c(
        "Joints" = "gray20",
        "Faults" = "black"
      )
    ),
    lwd = "structure",
    lwd.scale = tm_scale_categorical(
      values = c(
        "Joints" = 1,
        "Faults" = 2
      )
    ),
    col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Structure"),
    lwd.legend = tm_legend(show = FALSE) # Suppress separate line width legend block
  ) +
  
  # Park boundary
  tm_shape(park_boundary_3857, bbox = geology_aoi) +
  tm_polygons(fill_alpha = 0, col = "seagreen", lwd = 0.5)

# ---- 1. Carbon-14 corrected age map --------------------------------------

c14_geology_map <- geology_base +
  tm_shape(
    zion_samples_sf %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(c14_corr_age)), 
    bbox = sample_aoi
  ) +
  tm_symbols(
    shape = 21,
    fill = "c14_corr_age",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis"),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "C14 age (yr)"),
    size = 1,
    col = "black",
    lwd = 1
  ) +
  tm_title("Carbon-14 corrected age vs. Navajo Sandstone/faults/joints") +
  tm_layout(
    legend.out.side = TRUE,
    legend.out.side.position = "right"
  )

c14_geology_map

# ---- 2. Tritium mixing (young/modern fraction) -----------------------------
# ---- 2. Tritium-derived young-water fraction map --------------------------

tritium_geology_map <- geology_base +
  tm_shape(
    zion_samples_sf %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(young_fraction_capped)), 
    bbox = geology_aoi
  ) +
  tm_symbols(
    shape = 21,
    fill = "young_fraction_capped",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "-RdYlBu"),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Young (modern)\nwater fraction"),
    size = 1,
    col = "black",
    lwd = 1
  ) +
  tm_title("Tritium-derived young-water fraction vs. Navajo Sandstone/faults/joints") +
  tm_layout(
    legend.out.side = TRUE,
    legend.out.side.position = "right"
  )

tritium_geology_map

# ---- 3. Specific conductivity ----------------------------------------------
cond_geology_map <- geology_base +
  tm_shape(zion_samples_sf %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(cond)), 
           bbox = geology_aoi) +
  tm_symbols(
    shape = 21,
    fill = "cond",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis"),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Specific conductivity\n(uS/cm)"),
    size = 1, 
    col = "black", 
    lwd = 1) +
  tm_title("Specific conductivity vs. Navajo Sandstone/faults/joints") +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE, 
            legend.outside.position = "right")

cond_geology_map

# Arrange into a 3-row vertical stack or a 1x3 horizontal layout
combined_figure <- tmap_arrange(
  c14_geology_map, 
  tritium_geology_map, 
  cond_geology_map, 
  ncol = 1 # Use ncol = 3 for side-by-side, or ncol = 2 for a 2x2 grid style
)

# Display in RStudio viewer or R Markdown / Quarto
combined_figure

tmap_save(
  combined_figure, 
  filename = "data/park/ZION/zion_hydrochem_maps.png", 
  width = 10, 
  height = 14, 
  dpi = 600
)

```

The main canyon springs cluster tightly (δ¹⁸O ≈ -12.6 to -14.6‰), well
below the single local rain sample (Birch Creek precipitation, δ¹⁸O = -1.7‰)
and closer to the one available winter snow sample (SNOW PILE NEAR WEEPING
ROCK, δ¹⁸O = -15.85‰) -- consistent with winter-precipitation-dominated
recharge, similar in kind to CEBR. Notably, these values are essentially
unchanged between the 1988-89 samples and the 2023/2025 resampling at the
same sites (e.g., The Grotto, Weeping Rock, Refrigerator Spring), which is
itself evidence of a large, well-mixed reservoir rather than one tracking
year-to-year precipitation.

##### ---- Groundwater Flow Paths and Travel Time

As a cross-check on the carbon-14 ages, we estimate a plausible travel time
between the East Entrance and Lower Grotto springs using the regional
Navajo aquifer hydraulic gradient (from the well contours above) and a
literature range of hydraulic conductivity and porosity for sandstone.



```{r snow_rain_analysis}
# ============================================================
# Zion Canyon stable isotopes: snow vs. rain recharge mixing model
# ============================================================
#
# Two-endmember linear mixing model on d-excess (d = delta_2H - 8*delta_18O).
# Snow and rain precipitation samples within the Zion isotope dataset have
# strongly distinct d-excess signatures, so d-excess alone can be used to
# estimate what fraction of each non-precipitation sample's water traces to
# a snowmelt- vs. rain-dominated recharge signal:
#
#     f_snow = (d_excess_sample - d_excess_rain) / (d_excess_snow - d_excess_rain)
#     f_rain = 1 - f_snow
#
# This assumes each sample's d-excess is a simple two-component mix of the
# snow and rain endmembers, with no additional fractionation (e.g. from
# evaporation) along the flow path. That assumption is checked below via
# the mixing_flag column -- samples with f_snow outside [0, 1] have a
# d-excess more extreme than either endmember, which a simple mix cannot
# produce, and are more likely showing an evaporation signal (evaporation
# lowers d-excess) than a true rain-dominated signal.
#
# Builds on `isotopes` as loaded and spatially filtered in the
# `stable_isotopes` chunk above.
# ============================================================

# ---- 1. Endmembers ----
# Identified from the two precipitation (Sample_Type == "P") rows in the
# filtered Zion dataset:
#   Snow: "SNOW PILE NEAR WEEPING ROCK" (1/27/87)  d_excess = 16.8
#   Rain: "Birch Creek Precipitation"   (9/12/23)  d_excess = -10.3
d_excess_snow <- 16.8
d_excess_rain <- -10.3

# ---- 2. Mixing model ----
isotopes <- isotopes %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    f_snow = (d_excess_calculated - d_excess_rain) / (d_excess_snow - d_excess_rain),
    f_rain = 1 - f_snow,
    f_snow_clipped = pmin(pmax(f_snow, 0), 1),   # bounded 0-1 for mapping/plotting
    f_rain_clipped = 1 - f_snow_clipped,
    recharge_class = dplyr::case_when(
      Sample_Type == "P"           ~ NA_character_,
      f_snow >= 0.5                ~ "Snow-dominant",
      f_snow <  0.5                ~ "Rain-dominant"
    ),
    mixing_flag = dplyr::case_when(
      Sample_Type == "P"                 ~ NA_character_,
      f_snow < 0 | f_snow > 1            ~ "Outside 0-1: likely evaporated or non-binary signal",
      TRUE                                ~ "Within mixing range"
    )
  )

# ---- 3. Quick summary ----
isotopes %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::filter(Sample_Type != "P") %>%
  dplyr::count(recharge_class, mixing_flag)

# QA check: f_snow and f_rain should trace straight, complementary lines
# through the two endmembers (f_snow = 1 / f_rain = 0 at the snow sample;
# f_snow = 0 / f_rain = 1 at the rain sample), including precipitation rows.
ggplot(isotopes, aes(x = d_excess_calculated)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = f_rain, color = "rain")) +
  geom_point(aes(y = f_snow, color = "snow")) +
  theme_bw()

# ---- 4. Export ----
isotopes %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::filter(Sample_Type != "P") %>%
  dplyr::select(Location, Sample_Type, Source, Collection_Date,
                d_excess_calculated, f_snow, f_snow_clipped, f_rain_clipped,
                recharge_class, mixing_flag) %>%
  readr::write_csv("data/park/ZION/Stable_Isotopes/snow_rain_mixing_results.csv")




```


```{r flow_paths}

# Calculate hydraulic gradient in Navajo Aquifer -- based on Navajo contours
# to the east of the canyon where gw flow is essentially directly west.

# TODO / needs a look before this chunk will run: `navajo_gw` (built in the
# nwis_gw chunk via add_gw_meta()) is SITE metadata only -- aquifer code,
# drainage area, well depth, etc. -- and does not have a `mean_lev_va`
# column, so the line below will error as written. The actual water-level
# values live in `navajo_gw_lev` / `navajo_gw_and_springs` as `gw_elev_ft`.
# Likely fix: filter `navajo_gw_and_springs` (or `navajo_gw_lev`) to these
# two site_no values and difference `gw_elev_ft` instead of `mean_lev_va`
# -- left as-is rather than guessing, since picking the right two wells and
# confirming they're on a west-directed flow line is a domain call.
# Select 2 wells near east entrance
n_wells_grad <- navajo_gw %>%
  dplyr::filter(site_no %in% c("USGS-371400112523001", "USGS-371330112404001"))

# Calculate delta_h and delta_x
d_h <- (n_wells_grad[1,]$mean_lev_va - n_wells_grad[2,]$mean_lev_va)*0.3048 # in meters
d_x <- st_distance(n_wells_grad)[2,1] %>% as.numeric()

# Calculate hydraulic gradient
east_ent_grad <- d_h/d_x

# East Entrance to Lower Grotto distance
ee_lg_dist <- source_table_locs %>%
  dplyr::filter(wsd_source_id %in% c("ZION_WS_005_01", "ZION_WS_003_02")) %>%
  st_distance() %>%
  .[2,1] %>%
  as.numeric()

mapview(source_table_locs %>%
          dplyr::filter(wsd_source_id %in% c("ZION_WS_005_01", "ZION_WS_003_02")), zcol = "wsd_source_id")

# Range of hydraulic conductivity for sandstone in meters per day
K_range <- c(.003, .5, 1)  * .3048 # ft/d converted to m/d

# Porosity range
n_range <- c(0.06, 0.3)

# Darcy travel-time estimate: distance a parcel of groundwater could plausibly
# travel given the gradient/K/porosity combination and an elapsed time equal
# to the carbon-14 age. Compared against the observed East Entrance-to-Lower
# Grotto distance (ee_lg_dist) as a rough plausibility check on the C-14 ages.
gw_dist <- function(grad, K, n, delta_t) {
  K * grad * (1/n) * delta_t
}

# East Entrance Well's carbon-14-corrected age, pulled from `c14_nps`
# (already loaded above) rather than hardcoded -- this was previously an
# undefined variable (`east_entrance_c14` was referenced but never created,
# which would error). Confirm this is the intended age to test: `c14_nps`
# carries the raw NPS-reported age; if you want the mass-balance- or
# Pearson-corrected age from the `carbon_14_kimball_and_christenson` chunk
# instead, swap the source here.
east_entrance_c14 <- c14_nps %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::filter(location == "East Entrance Well") %>%
  dplyr::pull(c14_corr_age) %>%
  dplyr::first()

travel_time_est <- gw_dist(grad = east_ent_grad,
                           K = K_range[3] * 365,
                           n = n_range,
                           delta_t = east_entrance_c14)

print(travel_time_est)

```




### 7. Current Monitoring and Water Supply Context

Section 6 addressed where the main canyon springs' water comes from and how
old it is. This section shifts to what is actually being monitored today --
observed discharge and well levels -- which is the input the eventual
demand-to-supply comparison (a later section) will be built on.

##### ---- Meter Data

This is the observed monthly average spring discharge record used later
for the historical demand-to-supply comparison. Because we have
direct meter records for the main canyon springs, no modeled/routed discharge
is needed for the historical period.

```{r meter_data}

 meter_dat <- clean_zion_meter_dat() %>%
      dplyr::filter(!meter_location_service %in% c("Lodge Use",
                                                   "BZTR Use",
                                                   "PTI Use",
                                                   "Springdale Use",
                                                   "Zion Park Operations",
                                                   "Total Zion NP Use")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gallons_per_month = monthly_diff,
                n_days = days_in_month(ym),
                avg_gallons_per_day = gallons_per_month/n_days)

use_dat <- meter_dat %>%
  dplyr::filter(grepl("Use", meter_location_service))

spring_dat <- meter_dat %>%
  dplyr::filter(grepl("Spring", meter_location_service),
                !meter_location_service %in% c("South Vault/ Springdale", "Springdale Use"))

ggplot(spring_dat,
       aes(x = ym, y = avg_gallons_per_day, color = meter_location_service)) +
  geom_line(lwd = 1) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Flow (avg. gpd)") +
  scale_color_colorblind()




# ---- Seasonal pattern by spring: monthly mean with min-max range ----------
# Collapses the full period of record down to a single "typical year" per
# spring -- calendar month on x, with the across-years mean as the line and
# the across-years min/max as a shaded ribbon (alpha 0.4), faceted one panel
# per spring. `free_y` scales because spring discharge magnitudes differ a
# lot site to site (small seeps vs. larger springs); a shared y-axis would
# flatten the smaller springs' seasonal signal to a near-flat line. Wylie
# Sandtrap/Spring is dropped here (data quality/coverage issue, per KEC) and
# replaced below with a Virgin River panel for context.
spring_dat_monthly <- spring_dat %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(avg_gallons_per_day),
                meter_location_service != "Wylie Sandtrap / Spring") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(month = lubridate::month(ym, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(meter_location_service, month) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    mean_gpd = mean(avg_gallons_per_day, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_gpd  = min(avg_gallons_per_day, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_gpd  = max(avg_gallons_per_day, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_years  = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ---- Virgin River panel (replaces Wylie Sandtrap/Spring) -------------------
# Reuses `nwis_select_discharge` -- the daily discharge record already
# pulled for the selected reference gage (USGS 09405501) in the "NWIS
# Surface Water" section above -- rather than re-downloading it here.
# Aggregated to monthly mean first (matching the spring meter data's native
# monthly resolution), then converted from cfs to gallons/day (1 cfs =
# 646,317 gal/day) so it sits on the same "Flow (avg. gpd)" axis as the
# spring panels, then summarized the same way (across-years mean/min/max by
# calendar month). Note the gage's period of record is unlikely to line up
# exactly with the spring meters' -- both a longer USGS record and possible
# gaps -- so treat this panel's seasonal shape as the useful comparison,
# not a claim that the two are covering identical years.
CFS_TO_GPD <- 646317

virgin_river_monthly <- nwis_select_discharge %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(discharge)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = lubridate::floor_date(date, "month")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(avg_gallons_per_day = mean(discharge, na.rm = TRUE) * CFS_TO_GPD,
                    .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(meter_location_service = "Virgin River (USGS 09405501)",
                month = lubridate::month(ym, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(meter_location_service, month) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    mean_gpd = mean(avg_gallons_per_day, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_gpd  = min(avg_gallons_per_day, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_gpd  = max(avg_gallons_per_day, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_years  = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

spring_dat_monthly <- dplyr::bind_rows(spring_dat_monthly, virgin_river_monthly)

ggplot(spring_dat_monthly, aes(x = month, y = mean_gpd, group = meter_location_service)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = min_gpd, ymax = max_gpd), alpha = 0.4, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue4", lwd = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ meter_location_service, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Flow (avg. gpd)",
       title = "Seasonal pattern in spring discharge and Virgin River flow")
       #subtitle = "Monthly mean (line) with min-max range (ribbon); record period varies by site")

```

##### ---- Taylor Creek

The Taylor Creek well is a supply well for the Kolob Visitor center. Transducer data, i.e., groundwater level data, are available from April 2024 to July 2025. Here, we import and plot this data.

```{r taylor_creek}

tc_elev_ft <- sample_locs %>% 
  dplyr::filter(location == "Taylor Creek Well") %>% 
  .$elevation / 0.3048

tc_well <- read_csv("data/park/ZION/VuSitu/VuSitu_Log_2024-04-24_10-28-35_Taylor_Creek_Well_Zion_NP_Log_2024-04-24.csv",
                    skip = 25,
                    col_types = c("T","d","d","d")) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  rename_with(~ str_remove(., "_.*"),
              .cols = contains("_")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(elevation = tc_elev_ft - depth)

ggplotly(
ggplot(tc_well, aes(x = date, y = elevation)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Taylor Creek Well Depth (ft)")
)

```
